input.description: Check whether the fixer changed the builder

content.text:
Short answer: not yet — and one thing I found changes the risk calculus.

**This isn't the cleanup we scoped. It's a live P0.** The worker assigns its assembled system prompt once after building the session. `AgentSession.prompt()` reassigns `agent.state.systemPrompt` on *every* call — to whatever a `before_agent_start` handler returns, or back to pi's base prompt when nothing returns one. Lobu registered no handler, so the assignment was overwritten before the first request was ever built.

I proved it by reading the outgoing provider request, not the composed string:

```
=== WHAT THE MODEL RECEIVED (before fix) ===
contains Lobu prompt:  false
contains pi opener:    true
contains pi docs block: true
```

So in production every agent has been running on pi's stock *"You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness"* prompt — no identity, no soulMd/userMd, no platform instructions, no MCP server instructions, no memory guidance, no network section, plus a pi documentation block pointing at `node_modules` paths that don't exist in the worker image. That's the real answer to "why does the agent get pi docs?" — the regex was never the problem, its output just never arrived.

Fixed natively: the resource loader supplies the document as pi's `customPrompt`, and a hand-built synthetic `before_agent_start` extension reinstalls it each turn. No regex, no mutation of pi internals. `replaceBasePromptIdentity` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_OPENER_RE` are deleted.

**On confidence:** high (90) that delivery is fixed — mutation 4 restores the old assign-once shape and 4 tests fail; restoring each seam individually fails its own tests. But only medium (65) on prompt *content* in production, and that's the number that matters here: this changes the system prompt for every agent in the fleet, and I have not booted the app and driven a real conversation. Everything so far is a stubbed provider endpoint.

**On admin-merging:** yes once the required checks report green — that's your normal step 9, and I'll do it without asking. What I won't do is `--admin` past a check that hasn't reported. But I'd rather not merge on today's evidence at all, because the blast radius is every agent and my verification is offline. One real boot converts that 65 into a real number and costs maybe fifteen minutes.

    * fix(server): tell every chat agent it is a participant, not an observer
    
    A chat agent needs two facts nothing else in the prompt supplies: who it
    is in the conversation, and that the messages it receives are addressed
    to it. Only Slack supplied them — `createPlatformAdapter` attached an
    instruction provider solely when the platform descriptor declared one,
    and Slack is the only descriptor that does. Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp,
    Teams and Google Chat got an empty `platformInstructions`.
    
    With that gap the agent has only its identity markdown, which describes
    the principal in the third person ("you work on the user's data on their
    behalf") and never says the person currently typing IS that principal.
    The model resolves the ambiguity per turn, and often the wrong way: it
    treats the inbound message as observed conversation about a third party
    and narrates it back — "Burak is asking if REVERTCHECK is working. How
    would you like to respond?" — addressing an operator who does not exist.
    
    Make identity the default for every chat platform rather than a
    per-platform opt-in, so a new platform inherits it instead of
    re-deriving it. Slack keeps only its genuine delta, `<@U…>` mention
    encoding, and inherits the rest.
    
    Identity is best-effort: `Adapter.botUserId` is optional in the Chat SDK
    and some platforms carry no handle, so the participation framing is
    emitted even when no handle resolves — that is the half that fixes the
    voice. The only case that emits nothing is a missing org, which is the
    cross-tenant guard.

    id) and sits at the front of `gatewayInstructions`, where the
    openai-completions path caches by longest common prefix with no explicit
    breakpoints. A test renders it for two users/sessions on one connection
    and asserts byte equality, so a later conversation-scoped interpolation
    fails the build instead of silently costing the cache on every new

    Pins the degradation with a test: identity resolution has no agent+platform
    fallback because there is one InstructionContext construction site and it
    always carries the signed connectionId, so a missing field drops the handle

fix(agent-worker): deliver Lobu's system prompt to the model

The worker assembled a system prompt — agent identity, identityMd/soulMd/
userMd, platform instructions, MCP server instructions, memory guidance,
network access, skills, runtime shell — and assigned it once to
`session.agent.state.systemPrompt` after constructing the session.

`AgentSession.prompt()` reassigns that field on EVERY call: to whatever a

to pi's own base prompt. Lobu registered no handler, so the assignment was
overwritten before the first request was ever built. Every agent ran on
pi's stock "expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent
harness" prompt plus a documentation block describing pi's SDK, extensions
and TUI, pointing at node_modules paths that do not exist in the worker
image. None of the composed prompt reached the model.

Install it through the two seams pi actually consults: the resource
loader's `getSystemPrompt()` (pi's `customPrompt`, which replaces the
default rather than competing with it) and a synthetic `before_agent_start`
extension built in memory, which survives the per-turn reset. Both call one
renderer, so the base and per-turn documents cannot drift; the loader is
also the fail-safe, since the extension runner swallows handler errors — a

no longer patches pi's prompt text; it supplies the document.

prompt test asserted the string the worker *composed*, which is a different
question, and that difference is what hid this.

name: project-system-prompt-override-is-inert
description: "FIXED #2319 — pi resets agent.state.systemPrompt on EVERY prompt(); Lobu's assign-once was discarded before the first model call, so prod ran on pi's stock coding-harness prompt"
metadata:

---

**FIXED** by #2319 (squash `b8e66f022a18d491d405ad19e844a9527d0b5560`), the last
of #2313 → #2317 → #2319. Prod rollout verification OWED.

## The bug (was live in prod, not a cleanup)

`session-runner.ts` assigned `session.agent.state.systemPrompt` once after
`buildAgentSession()`. pi 0.73.x `AgentSession.prompt()` unconditionally
reassigns that field on EVERY call — to a **pi extension** `before_agent_start`
handler's return value, else back to `_baseSystemPrompt`. Lobu registered no
such extension (`runtimePluginHost.beforeAgentStart` only prepends to the USER
prompt), so identity + gateway tail (platform, MCP-server instructions, memory,
network, skills) were wiped before the first model call. Every agent ran on
pi's stock "expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness"
prompt plus a pi-docs block citing `node_modules` paths absent from the worker
image. That — not the regex — is why agents got pi docs.

Same reason #2318's participation block was inert on merge: it appends to
`gatewayInstructions`, part of the discarded payload.

## The fix — two seams, one renderer

`packages/agent-worker/src/runtime/system-prompt.ts` renders the document;
`pi-resources.ts` installs it twice:
1. `ResourceLoader.getSystemPrompt()` → pi's `customPrompt`. **Returns the
   body only** — pi appends its own `Current date:` / `Current working
   directory:` on this path, so returning the full document duplicates them.
2. A synthetic `before_agent_start` `Extension` built in memory (never loaded

Prod already runs a real agent turn as a **Helm post-upgrade smoke gate**: `POST /api/internal/smoke/dispatch` inserts a synthetic `chat_message` run, the worker spawns and executes end-to-end, and if `agent_transcript_snapshot` doesn't reach `terminal_status='completed'` in the window, **Helm rolls the release back**.

So the rollout itself is an e2e of the worker path on my change. If the new prompt wiring broke session boot, prod would roll back rather than advance — meaning "deployed SHA contains my merge commit" is already a real end-to-end pass signal, not just a deploy marker. That part I can gate on with a fully detached script, zero Claude involvement.

What it doesn't cover is prompt *content* — that a prod agent's reply actually reflects the Lobu identity and not pi's harness framing. That needs reading a transcript, which needs prod data access.

One decision from you, since it changes what I build:

#!/bin/bash
# Post-rollout verification + teardown for PR #2319
# (fix(agent-worker): deliver Lobu's system prompt to the model).
#
# Runs fully detached — survives the Claude session that created it.
#
# What "verified" means here: prod's Helm post-upgrade hook dispatches a
# synthetic chat_message run through the real worker pipeline and rolls the
# release BACK unless agent_transcript_snapshot reaches
# terminal_status='completed'. So a deployed revision that contains the squash
# commit is proof a real agent turn ran end-to-end on this change — not merely
# that the image shipped.
#
# Pass  -> tear down the worktree + local branch, exit 0, no Claude.
# Fail  -> leave everything intact and resume the originating Claude session.

set -uo pipefail

MERGE_SHA=b8e66f022a18d491d405ad19e844a9527d0b5560
BRANCH=feat/worker-owns-system-prompt
REPO=/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu
WORKTREE=$REPO/.claude/worktrees/worker-owns-system-prompt
SESSION=3bbf7a8f-aa32-4ddf-8a73-1d63870a1171
CLAUDE=/opt/homebrew/bin/claude
HEALTH=https://app.lobu.ai/health
BASELINE=30a4bd836fefb14569e20e7edac7e1055f5c9b7a   # prod revision at merge time

MAX_ATTEMPTS=30      # 30 x 3min = 90min
INTERVAL=180

cd "$REPO" || exit 1

log() { echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }

fail() {
  log "FAIL: $1"
  log "Worktree and branch left intact for investigation."
  # -p so the resumed session gets a concrete instruction, not a bare wake-up.
  "$CLAUDE" --resume "$SESSION" -p "Prod verification for PR #2319 FAILED: $1

Deployed revision never came to contain squash commit $MERGE_SHA within 90 minutes of merge, or prod moved to a revision that excludes it (possible Helm rollback — the post-upgrade smoke hook rolls back when the synthetic agent run does not reach terminal_status='completed').

Investigate whether the system-prompt change broke worker session boot. Do not tear down the worktree at $WORKTREE. Full log: /tmp/lobu-verify-2319.log" </dev/null >> /tmp/lobu-verify-2319.log 2>&1
  exit 1
}

log "watching for $MERGE_SHA (baseline $BASELINE)"

for i in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
  sleep $INTERVAL
  git fetch -q origin 2>/dev/null

  DEPLOYED=$(curl -s --max-time 20 "$HEALTH" | grep -oE '"revision":"[a-f0-9]+"' | cut -d'"' -f4)
  if [ -z "$DEPLOYED" ]; then
    log "attempt $i: health unreachable"
    continue
  fi

  if git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED" 2>/dev/null; then
    log "PASS: deployed=$DEPLOYED contains $MERGE_SHA"
    log "Helm post-upgrade smoke gate passed => a real agent turn completed end-to-end on this change."
    break
  fi

  # Prod moved somewhere that does NOT contain the merge. Advancing past it is
  # fine (any later main commit contains it); landing elsewhere means a revert
  # or rollback, which should not wait out the full window.
  if [ "$DEPLOYED" != "$BASELINE" ]; then
    fail "prod moved to $DEPLOYED, which does not contain $MERGE_SHA (revert or rollback)"
  fi

  log "attempt $i: deployed=$DEPLOYED (not yet)"

  if [ "$i" -eq "$MAX_ATTEMPTS" ]; then
    fail "timed out after 90 minutes; prod still on $DEPLOYED"
  fi
done

# ---- teardown -------------------------------------------------------------
# Only reached on PASS. Never runs from inside the directory being removed.
log "tearing down"
git worktree remove --force "$WORKTREE" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/  /'
git worktree prune 2>&1 | sed 's/^/  /'
git branch -D "$BRANCH" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/  /'
log "DONE — #2319 verified in prod, worktree and branch removed. No further action needed."
exit 0

content.text:
Set up and running detached — PID 80114, independent of this session.

**What it does.** Every 3 minutes for up to 90: fetches origin, reads `revision` from `https://app.lobu.ai/health`, and runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor b8e66f022 <deployed>` — merge commit first, gated on the squash SHA rather than the branch head, which is the pair of traps that has silently held this gate open before.

**Why that's a real e2e and not just a deploy marker.** Prod's Helm post-upgrade hook dispatches a synthetic `chat_message` run into the runs queue; the MessageConsumer claims it, spawns the worker subprocess, and the release is rolled back unless `agent_transcript_snapshot` reaches `terminal_status='completed'`. A revision containing my commit therefore means a real agent turn booted a session and ran to completion on the new prompt path. If my change broke session boot, prod rolls back instead of advancing.

**On pass:** removes the worktree, prunes, deletes the local branch (the remote one GitHub already auto-deleted), logs DONE, exits. No Claude, nothing for you to do.

**On fail:** leaves the worktree and branch untouched and runs `claude --resume 3bbf7a8f… -p "<what failed>"` so this session picks it up with the specifics. Two failure paths, not one — the 90-minute timeout, and prod moving to a revision that *excludes* the merge, which is the rollback signature and fails fast rather than waiting out the window.

Verified before launching: syntax clean, merge SHA resolves locally, ancestry returns TRUE against `origin/main` and FALSE against the current prod baseline, and the health parse returns `30a4bd836…`.

Log: `/tmp/lobu-verify-2319.log`.

**One limit, stated plainly.** This proves the worker runs end-to-end on the new code. It does not read a prod agent's reply, so it doesn't independently confirm the prompt *text* is right in prod — that's the option you set aside, and it's the one thing this gate won't catch. Content correctness rests on the wire-level dump and the input-equivalence check against the old committed code, both done here.

**Confidence: 93.** Basis: red→green reproduced against committed code, the delivered document read off the wire, renderer inputs shown identical to the old call site's expressions, 808 agent-worker tests plus full CI green, `pi-review` 0 bugs / 0 blockers. The remaining 7 is prod prompt text, unobserved by choice.

You're done here — close the session whenever. The only thing that will pull you back is a failure.
